relevance_note: Single-patient case report: 'Whole exome sequencing identified a heterozygous de novo pathogenic variant of the TNFAIP3 gene (c. 1777 C>T in exon 7, p.Q593X)'.
method_note: Read the whole paper (no tables, no supplementary section); JSON assembled by a short Python script in the scratch directory, every value typed from my reading and every span checked verbatim by script. In scope: the proband ('patient') and her two parents, who were tested by whole exome sequencing and do not carry the variant; the paper never says which parent is mother or father, so they are labelled 'parent of patient' and 'parent of patient 2' with sex not reported, and get no variant rows. Not given rows: the maternal and paternal grandmothers (mentioned only to explain consanguinity, neither tested nor affected); patients from earlier reports mentioned only as counts or subgroups of review cohorts (Yu et al. ref 7: 61 patients, 10 de novo, 3 first considered lupus/CTD, 'two of whom had prominent mucosal ulcer involvement and the third with ... ALPS and HA20'; Aeschlimann et al. ref 8: 16 patients, 5 received IVIG, two with sinopulmonary infections and IgG subclass deficiency); the CVID-cohort carrier (ref 12) and ALPS-cohort carrier (ref 13), described only as 'a truncating TNFAIP3 mutation in their cohort' / 'a separate TNFAIP3 mutation'; and the somatic p.Q593X tumour reports (refs 14, 15). Variant printed as 'c. 1777 C>T' with a space after 'c.'; recorded as printed, no transcript printed. Variant type 'nonsense' from the authors' 'premature stop codon'. Onset recorded as 2.5 years (first lymphadenopathy), because the authors call lymphadenopathy and fevers 'the initial features of HA20'; atopic dermatitis and infections in the first year of life were not attributed to HA20 by the authors. Age at HA20 diagnosis not stated (referred for genetics at age 14, WES age not given), so 'not reported'. Vital status 'alive' rests on the present-tense report of the past year at age 15. Checklist judgments: oral and genital ulcers excluded from the explicit statement that mucosal ulcers were never a feature (broader absence); gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation left not reported. Cytopenia (autoimmune) marked observed from pancytopenia with thrombocytopenia plus positive anti-platelet antibodies; the authors do not call it autoimmune. CNS involvement marked observed from the meningitis work-up with CSF white-cell elevation and negative infectious tests; the authors do not name a CNS diagnosis. Elevated ferritin is recorded as a feature, but the CRP/ESR checklist item is not reported because CRP and ESR are not mentioned. Normal complement at 7.5 years and at 12-14 years and the later suppressed C3/C4/CH50 (ages 8-11) are different time points, not a contradiction; recorded as one observed row with the normal values in the detail. Neutropenia at 11 resolved after stopping MMF (possible drug effect) and hypogammaglobulinemia may be partly treatment-related, as the authors say; both recorded as observed as reported. No contradictions found within the paper.
